answer: One defense is a bonded identity registry: each agent locks collateral tied to a single verified principal and receives one vote. An attacker splitting into n aliases must post n squared times the collateral, yet every alias still casts just one vote. Double voting or collusion slashes all linked bonds, so the system holds even at the nadir of a bot epidemic. Auditors trace the shared funding through the karst of shell wallets, and a sable watchdog flags the cluster before it swings a grant. Cloning raises cost, never influence.
